title: Field lab chronicle: progressive quant & prompt pipeline strategy
content:
Objective:
This is a lab-style record from the field POC with a regional telecom customer. Goal was to find a safe, incremental quantization + prompt/pipeline strategy that reduces inference cost by >=30% while keeping customer-facing accuracy within a 2% BLEU-equivalent degradation on their ticket-summary task and maintaining 95th percentile latency under 220ms for single-turn queries (90-token payload).

Context / constraints:
- Customer uses a hybrid setup: low-latency front-end for live chat, batch summarization for nightly ticket digest. Must support hosted + dedicated fallbacks.
- Data sensitivity: logs are scrubbed, but no on-prem hardware allowed for this POC.
- Primary model family: LlamaX-13B family baseline (float16). We evaluated smaller open variants and quantized versions as candidate fallbacks.
- SLO targets: p95 <= 220ms for interactive, average nightly batch throughput >= 1k docs/min. Cost goal: -30% per-token.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Model variants: LlamaX-13B fp16 baseline, LlamaX-13B int8 (static post-training), LlamaX-13B progressive-mixed (per-layer 8->6 bits), LlamaX-7B-quantized (int8), and a distilled 6B float16.
- Serving configs: batch size 1 (stream), batch size 8 (micro-batch), persistent KV cache enabled/disabled, prefix caching for common ticket intros.
- Routing policies: always-primary, latency-first (route to 7B fallback if p95 projected > 220ms), cost-first (route to quantized variants unless quality drop detected).
- Prompt pipeline variants: (A) single-shot full-context prompt, (B) segmented prompt with retrieval + filter, (C) compressed prompt (entity-only + skeleton), (D) reranker + generate to apply minimal hallucination penalty.

Key findings (high level):
1) Progressive per-layer quantization (8->6 bits schedule applied during offline PTQ) gave the best quality/cost tradeoff. Perceptible quality drop only when layers 0-6 were pushed to 4 bits. 8->6 (most attention/ffn kept at 8, deeper layers at 6) reduced token cost by ~28% vs fp16 and p95 latency by ~18% under production-like load.

2) Static int8 PTQ delivered 32% token cost reduction but introduced a 4–7% task-specific accuracy regression on edge-case conversation summarization (rare entity abbreviations). For interactive flows this regression manifested as more frequent truncations and off-by-one entity expansions.

3) Smaller model fallback (7B) reduces latency dramatically for short prompts but fails on long-context summarization: ROUGE reduced by ~6% on 800–1200 token inputs. Good as first-pass for quick responses but not a universal fallback.

4) Prompt pipeline (B) retrieval + filter + compact prompt gave the largest consistent quality stability vs smaller token budgets. When combined with progressive quant, it kept customer-visible regressions <1.5% while enabling cost targets.

Microbench notes (representative numbers, internal perf harness):
- Baseline LlamaX-13B fp16, single-stream p95: 260ms (device: A100-80GB, default kernels), throughput single-core ~3.8 tok/s
- LlamaX-13B progressive 8->6, single-stream p95: 210ms, throughput ~4.5 tok/s
- LlamaX-13B int8 static, single-stream p95: 190ms, throughput ~5.0 tok/s
- LlamaX-7B int8, single-stream p95 on short prompts: 120ms
Notes: measurements include RPC overhead simulated to approximate hosted deployment. Enabling prefix cache reduced p95 by additional ~10–12ms for common templates.

Quality diagnostics (examples):
- Failure patterns for int8: occasional factual drift on low-frequency tokens (model substituted rare acronyms). Suspect numeric underflow in select layer matmul kernels post-quant.
- Progressive mixed: mostly preserved semantics; minor fluency artifacts when large compressive prompts used (lossy prompt compression amplifies quant artifacts).

Prompt engineering tactics tested (with results):
- Entity-first skeletoning: extract named entities and feed as structured preamble + short context. Result: smaller prompts, robustness preserved, better for quantized models.
- Two-stage rerank+generate: generate N=4 candidates on a cheaper 7B quantized model, rerank with a light-weight scorer on the 13B progressive model. Result: overall quality matched baseline while saving ~22% cost. Latency increased slightly for worst-case paths; needs asynchronous trajectories for live chat.
- Dynamic instruction scaling: reduce instructional overhead for short interactions; increases consistency under quantization.

An example pipeline (recommended for POC):
1) Ingest -> ner + canonicalize -> retrieval top-3 (doc snippets) -> skeletonize (entities+one-sentence extract) -> light preamble + user query -> route to progressive-quant 13B for generation.
2) If latency budget tight (p95 projection > 200ms) -> fallback: 7B-quant generate N=4 -> rerank on 13B progressive (scoring only, cheaper KV-enabled path).
3) Nightly batch: use full 13B int8 static with larger batch sizes (32–64) where throughput matters more than strict p95.

Operational notes and caveats:
- Canary rollout: start with 5% of traffic to progressive-quant, collect metrics for accuracy regressions using the customer-supplied eval set (shot noise: 500 cases). Gate promotion by regression <2% and latency < SLO.
- Monitoring: set up prompt-level diffs (gold vs model) and token-level delta cost dashboards. Add alerts for entity hallucination spikes and for reranker mismatch rate > 7%.
- Safety: quantized kernels changed logits distribution slightly; re-run safety classifiers on generated text in canary.
- Reproducibility: store quantization seeds, PTQ calibration corpus snapshot, and per-layer scale tables in the artifact store (linked artifacts).

Decision log (what we decided for next-phase POC):
- Adopt progressive per-layer quant schedule as primary optimization path (safe middle ground).
- Implement pipeline (retrieval + skeletonize + progressive-quant 13B) as default serving chain for interactive flows.
- Use 7B quantized as fast fallback with reranker flow for tail-latency events.
- Reserve static int8 13B for nightly batch pipeline where throughput is primary.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Investigate kernel-level numeric stability for static int8 on rare-token regression. Assign to infra: Miguel + Rowan. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-3241.
- Evaluate on a larger customer eval set (2k cases) before moving beyond 20% traffic.
- Explore per-customer calibration of quant thresholds (could be automated by Redwood Optimize in future).

Appendix: short examples (input -> preferred output notes)
- Input (short): "Ticket: user cannot authenticate after password reset. Logs: JWT-expire 401."
  Preferred: concise summary + suggested triage steps. Both progressive-quant and rerank flow matched baseline. Static int8 occasionally omitted the numeric code in the second sentence.

- Input (long): 1,200-token support thread with interleaved system logs.
  Preferred: condensed 6-bullet summary retaining 3 action items. Progressive-quant kept all three; 7B fallback missed a low-frequency log line leading to incomplete action list.

Next steps for the team:
- Build small canary deployment for progressive-quant 13B with ramp schedule and observability hooks (end-to-end request tracing, per-prompt cost). Owner: Priya.
- Kernel debug work on int8 PTQ instability (infra + applied-ml). Owner: Miguel, Rowan.
- Customer workshop to show live comparisons and get acceptance criteria for promotion. Owner: Aisha.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep more samples of long-thread summarization in the eval set; that's where smaller models fail fastest.
- Consider a midweight 10B candidate if customer willing to entertain an additional model variant; may avoid some 7B failure modes while still saving cost vs 13B fp16.

End of chronicle.
